signals.notes: formula does not fit this van's reply (Exception calling "Replace" with "3" argument(s): "formula needs byte B, response has 1"); [DIFFERS FROM LIBRARY] WiCAN expression ([B4:B5]/256)/10. Library/OBDb and Lightning list: A/20+6 (A*0.05+6). These cannot both be right. For 12.6 V, A/20+6 needs A=132, which this formula reads as about 13.2 V only if B is 0. Probably a WiCAN profile error; trust A/20+6.

CONFLICTS with OBDb (A/20+6, 8-bit) and the user's PIDs.md ([B4:B5]). Example: A=0x90 (144) gives 14.4 V with this formula and 13.2 V with OBDb's. OBDwiz showed V_BATT_BCM 14.4 V at idle (https://github.com/anthonysecco/WiCAN-Ford-Transit/blob/main/obdwiz.md), but no raw bytes were captured. Check against a DMM with the engine off and running.

signals.name: TPMS last received sensor ID
signals.vehicles: Focus RS Mk3; Mach-E scan shows 9 data bytes
signals.notes: Multi-frame response. Layout per openRS: ID(4) pressure(2) temp(1) status(1) checksum(1). Match the ID against 280F-2812 to find which wheel the temp/pressure belongs to. The library only has the temp byte (G-40).

signals.name: TPMS last received sensor pressure

signals.name: Left front tire pressure (alternate formula)
signals.notes: openRS says it validated this against known tire pressures. Same formula in the F-150 Gen14 Torque list (https://www.f150gen14.com/forum/attachments/exported-pids-20221207-txt.65935/). The F-150 Lightning sheet uses the equivalent ((A*256)+B+22)*0.048. This works out to about (raw+22)/20.7 psi, so it is roughly 1 psi higher than the library's raw/20 at normal pressures. Raw is likely kPa*3 with an offset. scan tool unit is kPa.; converted from the source's psi

signals.name: Tire pressure, left front
signals.vehicles: Focus RS MK3 (validated by openRS), F-250/F-350 6.7L, F-150 Lightning, Torque community
signals.notes: [DIFFERS FROM LIBRARY] Library/OBDb: raw/20 psi. WiCAN issue #642 (F-350): raw*0.05 psi, the same. WiCAN focus_rs profile: raw/10/2.036 psi, nearly the same. This Torque formula is about 0.0483*raw + 1.06 psi, so it reads about 0.3 psi lower at 35 psi. The WiCAN transit.json and the user's raw/10 is inHg.; converted from the source's psi

signals.name: Left Front Tire Pressure

signals.name: TPMS left front tire pressure (Ford kPa formula)
signals.notes: Raw Transit response 62 28 13 04 90 (raw 1168) decodes to 57.5 psi, or 396.7 kPa before the *0.145. The post's version adds /14.504 to output bar. For comparison, (A*256+B)/20 gives 58.4 psi and PIDs.md's /10 gives 116.8 ('inHg' label, about 57.4 psi). So /20 psi, /10 inHg and this kPa formula all agree within about 1 psi. Same scaling applies to 2814-2818, 2827 and 2828.; converted from the source's psi

signals.name: TPMS left front tire pressure (cross-check, Super Duty)
signals.vehicles: F-350 Super Duty (same BCM DID set as Transit)
signals.notes: Raw 07E8 05 62 28 13 04 BE (raw 1214) decodes to 60.7 psi, but the author's screen read 65.7 psi. The mismatch (factor 0.054) is unexplained: the readings may have been taken at different times. Same formula as OBDb (/20). The issue also uses 2814 for FR.; converted from the source's psi

signals.notes: fordreader: lat = int16(frame2 bytes 1-2)/60. With A = first byte after 62 80 12, that is bytes E,F. The same code's heading = N,O matches the library's bix 104. Resolution is about 1 arcminute (~1.8 km). F-150 Lightning users report poor precision (https://www.f150lightningforum.com/forum/threads/pid-for-gps-coordinates.14798/). Finer fractional minutes may be in neighboring bytes (C/D, G/H), undecoded.

signals.name: GPS longitude
signals.notes: fordreader: lon = int16(frame2 bytes 5-6)/60 -> bytes I,J. Same precision caveat as latitude. APIM PIDs include GPS_LATITUDE, GPS_LONGITUDE, GPS_ALTITUDE, GPS_HEADING, GPS_SPEED, GPS_FIX. GPS_FIX is probably also in 8012 but unlocated.

signals.name: GPS latitude
signals.notes: [NEW SIGNAL on known DID] Library has altitude (A-B), speed (bix 88) and heading (N-O, which agrees with fordreader). fordreader reads lat from bytes E-F and lon from I-J as signed/60. That resolution is only 1 minute, so the fractional part is likely in nearby bytes; check before relying on it.

signals.name: GPS longitude
signals.notes: [NEW SIGNAL on known DID] See latitude entry.

signals.name: SYNC GPS altitude
signals.notes: Name-based mapping to OBDb TRANSIT_SYNC_GPS_ALTITUDE (bytes A-B). OBDwiz on the user's van also shows GPS_LATITUDE_APIM, GPS_LONGITUDE_APIM, GPS_FIX_APIM ('3D Fix'), GPS_HEADING_APIM and GPS_SPEED_APIM, so a position fix is readable over OBD. Lat/long DIDs not found; they are possibly in the same 8012 record (not verified).

signals.name: SYNC GPS speed
signals.notes: OBDb byte offset 11 (bix 88) gives bytes L-M, and OBDb applies *3.6. Check the response length first; with the WiCAN 'B4' convention, L is B15.

signals.name: SYNC GPS heading
signals.notes: OBDb bix 104 gives bytes N-O. OBDwiz read 11°.

signals.name: Learned octane ratio / octane adjust ratio (OAR)
signals.vehicles: 2011-13 Taurus SHO 3.5 EcoBoost; 2011 Focus (cross-check); F-150 2021 PowerBoost
signals.notes: Resolves ratio-vs-% conflict: raw is signed16/16384 = -1..+1 (-1 = best fuel, timing fully advanced per Cobb convention). scan tool shows it as a positive percent = -ratio*100: poster's pairs 0xDCEC=54.81% and 0xD145=73.01% match -(signed16/16384)*100 exactly. Mustang6g users sometimes divide by -16384 to flip the sign (https://www.mustang6g.com/forums/goto/post?id=2387412). Gen14 F-150 users report -0.7 to -1.0 on 93 octane. Same formula also in f150gen14 Torque CSV.

signals.name: Ignition correction (knock retard), cylinder 1
signals.notes: [DIFFERS FROM LIBRARY] Library: signed raw/512. openRS divides by -512 so retard shows positive. Same magnitude, opposite sign.

signals.name: Knock / ignition timing correction (global spark retard)
signals.vehicles: 2010-13 Taurus SHO / Flex 3.5 EcoBoost; 2015+ Mustang GT 6R80; F-150 EcoBoost
signals.notes: Negative = timing being added (good), positive = knock retard (bad); range roughly -4..+7.5 deg. Some use /-512 to flip sign. Mustang6g equivalent: Signed(A)/2+(B/512) (https://www.mustang6g.com/forums/threads/knock-pid.86127/). Reads 0 if a tune sets knock control to per-cylinder. Library calls it 'Ignition correction, cylinder 1' with same /512 scaling.

signals.name: Purga del cánister
signals.notes: Name in Spanish as in source. 'verified' = verified by source author on their vehicle, not on Transit. Formula converted from JS arrow function (A,B = data bytes after 62 XX XX). Source note: EVAPCP, ciclo de trabajo de la electroválvula. CONFIRMADO el 17/09 en cuatro estados distintos: 100 % al ralentí caliente, 0 % subiendo de vueltas en punto muerto, 95 % rodando y 35 % en retención. Se mueve con todo, o sea que es un mando en vivo. Una purga pegada abierta mete vapores de gasolina sin control y es una causa clásica de ralentí inestable.

signals.name: Transmission fluid temperature
signals.vehicles: Taurus SHO 6F55; 2019+ Ranger 10R80; F-150 2021 PowerBoost 10R80; S550 Mustang; Explorer
signals.notes: Sources give °F: (((signed(A)*256)+B)*(9/8)+320)/10 which equals signed16/16 °C *1.8+32. Torque Pro built-in '[FORD]Transmission Temp' is this PID. Also: https://ecoboostperformanceforum.com/threads/torque-pids-take-2.3141/ and f150gen14 Torque CSV. Some Mustang posts omit signed(). Known in library; same scaling.

signals.name: Transmission fluid temperature (signed high byte)
signals.notes: Raw Transit responses: 62 1E 1C 01 2A gives 18.6 °C (65.5 °F, cold) and 62 1E 1C 04 07 gives 64.4 °C. The posted formula is the °F form ((signed(A)*256)+B)*9/80+32. The maintainer said WiCAN expressions can't use signed(), so use [B4:B5]/16 (unsigned) unless you need sub-zero readings. Issue #642 (F-350) uses the same scaling, ([B4:B5]*0.1125)+32 °F.
